text: Status: v0.3. Early but real — the full loop (search → live tree → apply) works today with Claude Code. A Codex CLI adapter ships too, but so far it has only been tested against a fake codex binary. Built in the open; star the repo to follow along, or jump in — early contributors shape the architecture. Python projects managed with uv: the value command runs inside fresh worktrees, which don't inherit your virtualenv — use command = "uv run pytest -q" (or pass --value "uv run pytest -q" ) so each worktree resolves its own environment. Turn any coding agent into a tree-searching agent. agent-mcts is an open-source (MIT) test-time search harness that wraps a coding agent CLI with Monte Carlo Tree Search. It is verified with Claude Code; see Supported agents for the rest. Instead of a single trajectory that either works or doesn't, your agent explores multiple solution branches, backtracks from dead ends, and concentrates budget on the most promising path. Not yet, on the tasks measured so far ( bench/ , v0.3.0, Claude Code with haiku , 5-episode budget). Each answer is scored on hidden tests the agent never sees, and compared with the first attempt of the same run, which is what a single agent run would have returned. Two harder tasks (npm semver ranges, ISO 8601 durations), 10 runs per setting: What the per-run numbers show: An earlier, smaller measurement on three easier tasks looked better (99% with the judge against 90% for a single attempt), but there every first attempt in the judge runs already scored 98% or more, so it never tested this case. Better judging is the next thing to work on ( full report ). Production coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, ...) run a single linear loop : act, observe, retry in place. No branching, no backtracking, no principled exploration. Research shows search helps: SWE-Search (ICLR 2025) reported a ~23% relative improvement on SWE-bench by adding MCTS on top of software agents. But that result lives in a research framework — there is no tool that brings it to the agent you already use. agent-mcts closes that gap: uv tool install agent-mcts cd your-project agent-mcts run " fix the flaky test in tests/test_auth.py " agent-mcts run --agent codex " fix the flaky test in tests/test_auth.py " # untested with the real Codex CLI The run auto-detects your installed agent and your test command, then shows the plan before spending anything: Agent: claude · Value: pytest -x -q · Budget: 12 nodes / $10.00 Proceed? [y/N] While searching, the tree grows live in your terminal (real output): task: fix the flaky test in tests/test_auth.py run 20260802-190219 · episodes 3/12 · cost $0.31/$10.00 ✓ n0 [r=0.00 Q=0.42 N=4] ├── ✓ n1 [r=0.67 Q=0.78 N=2] mocked the clock in the auth fixture │ └── ● n3 [r=? Q=0.00 N=0] expanding… └── ✗ n2 [r=0.00 Q=0.00 N=1] sleep-based fix (tests timed out) When it finishes (or when you Ctrl-C — MCTS is anytime, the partial tree is saved): agent-mcts show # inspect the tree; `show n3` prints a node's prompt, summary, evaluation agent-mcts resume # continue the latest run where it stopped (`resume -n 20` raises the budget) agent-mcts apply # stage the best node's changes (squash merge — you review and commit) agent-mcts apply n2 # ...or pick a different branch How it works ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ search engine │ UCT selection · expansion │ (agent-agnostic, Python) │ hybrid value fn · backup └──────────────┬──────────────┘ │ AgentBackend protocol ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ claude adapter codex adapter kimi adapter (claude -p) (codex exec) (kimi -p) verified fake-tested planned Node = (git worktree, agent session). Filesystem state branches via worktrees; conversation state branches via session forking (native on Claude Code, context-injection fallback elsewhere). Value function = your tests. Exit 0 scores 1.0; a failing run earns partial credit by pass ratio (read from pytest, jest, cargo test, go test and JUnit-style summaries), and the failing output is fed into children's revision prompts. pytest / npm test / make test are picked up automatically. Add --judge to have an LLM score each attempt's diff as well — see LLM judge . Every node is a git branch ( agent-mcts/<run>/<node> ), so apply is an ordinary squash merge and everything is auditable after the fact. Worktrees are disposable; branches are the record. Every state change is journaled (append-only jsonl per run), so an interrupted search is still a valid, inspectable tree. Supported agents Agent Headless Session fork Status Claude Code claude -p native ( --fork-session ) ✅ v0.1, verified Codex CLI codex exec --json context injection v0.2, tested only against a fake codex binary Kimi CLI kimi -p context injection planned (v0.4) Gemini CLI, OpenCode, ... adapter PRs welcome! Configuration Zero config required. When you need it, .agent-mcts.toml : agent = " claude " # or "codex" [ value ] command = " pytest tests/ -x -q " # exit code + pass ratio → score in [0, 1] judge = true # also score each attempt with an LLM judge [ search ] max_nodes = 20 # episode budget max_cost_usd = 10.0 parallelism = 3 # episodes in flight at once (`-j`) CLI flags ( --agent , -n , --max-cost , --value , --model , --agent-timeout , --judge/--no-judge , -j/--parallel ) override the file. Python projects managed with uv: the value command runs inside fresh worktrees, which don't inherit your virtualenv — use command = "uv run pytest -q" (or pass --value "uv run pytest -q" ) so each worktree resolves its own environment. Every option, the LLM judge , parallel runs , resuming and how failures, cost and timeouts are handled: docs/configuration.md . Search hyperparameters are first-class: this is built by an MCTS researcher and meant to double as a research harness for test-time search over real software tasks. This project is open source under the MIT license and developed fully in the open — issues, design discussions, and PRs all happen here on GitHub. Contributions are welcome from day one. The highest-impact contribution is an agent adapter : a few hundred lines implementing the AgentBackend protocol for your favorite CLI agent, with no need to touch the search core. Use the Claude Code adapter as the reference, and the fake-binary pattern in its tests to keep CI free of API calls. See CONTRIBUTING.md for setup. Also welcome: bug reports, docs, benchmark tasks, and arguing with our UCT constants. MIT — do whatever you want, just keep the notice.
